Charter Communications (CHTR) has a case for a 40% jump in its stock if Spectrum Mobile, its phone service, can help it stop losing Internet customers. A rise that size is not rare for these shares, which climbed 40% or more within the year in six of the last ten calendar years. Yet the stock fell 57.1% over the past year, while the S&P 500 gained 14.0%. You probably see a shrinking cable company. A fast-growing phone business sits inside it, and that is the contradiction. So how big has Spectrum Mobile become?

Spectrum Mobile Had Over 12.5 Million Lines In July

Charter added 1.7 million Spectrum Mobile lines over the twelve months to June 2026, marking growth of 16%, management said on the July 24, 2026 call. Management also called Charter the fastest-growing mobile provider in its footprint. The business has room left, too, as management said only about 20% of Charter's Internet customers also take its mobile service.

Separately, could Tesla make their product more tangible? See: How Musk's Massive Marketing Miss Cost Tesla $10 Trillion.

Cox gives Charter a new market for Spectrum Mobile. Charter completed its deal for Cox Communications on August 20, 2026, and said Spectrum pricing and packaging would launch in all Cox markets in mid-September. Management described mobile in the Cox footprint as very underpenetrated. Spectrum Mobile is adding lines fast so far, and most of Charter's customers have yet to take it.

Is Spectrum Mobile Keeping Charter's Internet Customers?

Spectrum Mobile helps keep the customers who take it, but it has not yet stopped Charter's overall losses. Internet customers who also buy Charter's mobile service leave nearly 40% less often than those who do not, management said on the July 24 call.

Yet the company lost 172,000 Internet customers in fiscal Q2 2026, counting homes and small businesses. Management tied the drop to fewer new connections, while churn, the rate at which customers leave, was essentially flat. Management named the competition behind the weak sign-ups, pointing to more fixed wireless, people using mobile instead of home Internet, and fiber overlap, with aggressive promotions from some rivals.

That is where the case for mobile falls short so far. The benefit of mobile, as management describes it, is that customers leave less often, but management named weaker sign-ups as the main reason for the Internet customer weakness. Management expects Charter to stabilize and return to broadband growth over time as the growth of new competition subsides, but that is a forecast, not a result.

title: T vs. GLW: Which Telecom Infrastructure Stock Is the Better Buy?

T vs. GLW: Which Telecom Infrastructure Stock Is the Better Buy?

GLW
VZ

Trading disclosure

AT&T, Inc. T and Corning Incorporated GLW are both prominent players in the U.S. telecommunications space. The companies operate in different segments of the telecom sector and are accelerating 5G and broadband infrastructure deployment across the country. The company is the second largest wireless service provider in North America and one of the world's leading communications service carriers. It provides wireless, local exchange, long-distance, broadband, Internet, video, managed networking, wholesale and cloud-based services. Corning is the leading supplier of optical fiber and connectivity solutions that support high-speed communications.

Per a report from Grand View Research, the U.S. Fiber to the Home market is projected to witness a 12.7% compound annual growth rate from 2025 to 2030. Let us delve deeper into the companies' competitive dynamics to see which is better positioned in this broader sector.

The Case for GLW

Corning is positioned to benefit from rising demand for optical connectivity as telecom operators and data center customers expand their networks. Its Optical Communications segment delivered a strong performance in the third quarter of 2026, with sales increasing 44% year over year to $2.38 billion and segment net income climbing 80% to $532 million.

Enterprise Networks was a key contributor, with sales advancing 84% to $1.53 billion as demand for AI-related connectivity products accelerated. Generative AI product sales more than doubled during the quarter. Carrier Networks also recorded growth, although at a more moderate 4%, supported by demand for data center interconnect solutions.

Customer commitments provide another source of support for the growth outlook. Corning secured four long-term, multibillion-dollar agreements during the quarter, including agreements with AT&T and Verizon Communications VZ.

However, investors should consider the risks alongside this growth opportunity. The more modest expansion in Carrier Networks sales shows that demand is not increasing uniformly across the communications business. Moreover, Corning must invest in capacity to meet customer requirements. Growing competition, supply-chain uncertainty and fluctuations in global economic conditions remain major concerns. However, beyond telecom, Corning boasts a comprehensive portfolio consisting of display solutions, consumer electronics, automotive and solar markets. Such a diverse portfolio reduces its vulnerability to any one sector.

Based on our proprietary calculation, trailing 12-month return on invested capital reached 10.8%, above Corning's 10-year median of 7.8%, its five-year median of 8.7% and three-year median of 8.6%, but slightly below the industry median of 11.2%. Higher optical volumes and operating leverage are helping returns recover as the company expands its AI connectivity platform.

title: Corning Falls 14.1% in the Past Month: Is the Pullback a Buying Chance?

Corning Falls 14.1% in the Past Month: Is the Pullback a Buying Chance?

Corning Incorporated GLW shares have fallen 14.1% in the past month, creating a sharp contrast with the company's improving earnings, optical growth and margin profile.

Zacks Investment Research

Image Source: Zacks Investment Research

The decline gives investors a more attractive entry point than a month ago, but it does not automatically make GLW inexpensive. Corning's AI-related growth is accelerating and profitability is improving, while solar execution, consumer-market weakness and a premium valuation leave room for further volatility.

Corning's Pullback Contrasts With Strong Growth

Corning's third-quarter operating performance moved in the opposite direction from its recent share price.

Core sales increased 19% year over year to $5.08 billion, while core earnings rose 36% to 91 cents per share. GAAP sales increased 18% to $4.86 billion and GAAP earnings advanced 56% to 78 cents per share.

The momentum is expected to extend into the fourth quarter. Management projects core sales of $5.2-$5.3 billion, representing approximately 19% year-over-year growth, with core earnings of 96 cents to $1 per share, up roughly 36%.

That operating trajectory provides a fundamental counterweight to the 14.1% stock decline.

GLW's AI Engine Keeps Expanding

Optical Communications remains Corning's clearest growth engine. Third-quarter segment sales jumped 44% year over year to $2.38 billion and segment net income increased 80% to $532 million. Enterprise Networks sales surged 84% to $1.53 billion, while Gen AI product sales more than doubled.

The opportunity is also becoming more visible through customer commitments. Corning secured four long-term, multibillion-dollar customer agreements during the third quarter, including agreements with Verizon Communication VZ and AT&T T. Management said these arrangements help underpin the growth expected under its Springboard plan.

Corning is targeting a $30 billion annualized sales run rate by the end of 2028 and $40 billion by the end of 2030, with earnings expected to grow faster than sales.

Corning's Margins Add Fundamental Support

Growth is translating into better operating efficiency.

Core gross margin expanded 150 basis points year over year to 40.5% in the third quarter. Core operating margin improved 310 basis points to 22.7%, while core return on invested capital rose 330 basis points to 16.7%. Adjusted free cash flow totaled $661 million during the quarter.

Through the first nine months of 2026, adjusted free cash flow reached $2.27 billion even as Corning continued investing in additional capacity to meet customer demand.

Those improvements matter because Corning's growth strategy requires sizable manufacturing investments. Higher margins and returns give the company more flexibility to fund expansion without relying entirely on top-line growth.

Direct-to-device services are already being used by SpaceX.

The proposed changes could give SpaceX more options to expand Starlink Mobile's coverage and capacity.

AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile have urged the FCC to exclude the 2.5 GHz and 3.45 GHz frequency bands from the proposed expansion.

SpaceX (SPCX) was in the spotlight on Thursday ahead of a key Federal Communications Commission (FCC) vote on proposals that could expand wireless spectrum access for satellite-to-phone services, potentially supporting the company's Starlink Mobile ambitions.

SPCX shares were down about 2% at the time of writing, tracking a broader sell-off in space stocks.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

What Is The FCC Voting On?

The FCC is set to consider two separate proposals on October 29. The first would pave the way for a future auction of 25 MHz of wireless spectrum for traditional cellular, satellite, or combined services.

The second would make an additional 482 MHz of spectrum eligible for direct-to-device services, which allow compatible smartphones to connect directly to satellites. This technology, already being used by SpaceX, is particularly useful in areas with limited or no cellular coverage.

The vote would advance the proposal but not grant satellite operators access to the additional spectrum.

How Could SpaceX Benefit?

The proposed changes could give SpaceX more options to expand Starlink Mobile's coverage and capacity. SpaceX has already been expanding its spectrum holdings. Earlier this month, the company agreed to acquire Grain Management's nationwide spectrum portfolio in the 800 MHz band, which could improve mobile connectivity over longer distances and inside buildings.

More recently, the FCC approved SpaceX's proposed acquisition of three spectrum licenses from Tristar, helping fill gaps in its U.S. wireless coverage.

AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile Oppose Expansion Proposal

AT&T, Verizon and T-Mobile, along with the Cellular Telecommunications and Industry Association, have urged the FCC to exclude the 2.5 GHz and 3.45 GHz frequency bands from the proposed expansion. The carriers argue that satellite transmissions could interfere with existing 5G networks used by more than 300 million people.

T-Mobile warned that such interference could reduce a cell tower's coverage area for signals sent from phones to the tower by as much as 96%.

Emcor Group (EME) came out with quarterly earnings of $9.6 per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $8.33 per share. This compares to earnings of $6.57 per share a year ago. These figures are adjusted for non-recurring items.

This quarterly report represents an earnings surprise of +15.25%. A quarter ago, it was expected that this construction and maintenance company would post earnings of $7.23 per share when it actually produced earnings of $9.06, delivering a surprise of +25.31%.

Over the last four quarters, the company has surpassed consensus EPS estimates four times.

Emcor Group, which belongs to the Zacks Building Products - Heavy Construction industry, posted revenues of $5.54 billion for the quarter ended September 2026, surpassing the Zacks Consensus Estimate by 6.52%. This compares to year-ago revenues of $4.3 billion. The company has topped consensus revenue estimates four times over the last four quarters.

The sustainability of the stock's immediate price movement based on the recently-released numbers and future earnings expectations will mostly depend on management's commentary on the earnings call.

Emcor Group shares have added about 10.9% since the beginning of the year versus the S&P 500's gain of 13.1%.

What's Next for Emcor Group?

While Emcor Group has underperformed the market so far this year, the question that comes to investors' minds is: what's next for the stock?

There are no easy answers to this key question, but one reliable measure that can help investors address this is the company's earnings outlook. Not only does this include current consensus earnings expectations for the coming quarter(s), but also how these expectations have changed lately.

Empirical research shows a strong correlation between near-term stock movements and trends in earnings estimate revisions. Investors can track such revisions by themselves or rely on a tried-and-tested rating tool like the Zacks Rank, which has an impressive track record of harnessing the power of earnings estimate revisions.

Ahead of this earnings release, the estimate revisions trend for Emcor Group was unfavorable. While the magnitude and direction of estimate revisions could change following the company's just-released earnings report, the current status translates into a Zacks Rank #4 (Sell) for the stock. So, the shares are expected to underperform the market in the near future. You can see the complete list of today's Zacks #1 Rank (Strong Buy) stocks here.

It will be interesting to see how estimates for the coming quarters and the current fiscal year change in the days ahead. The current consensus EPS estimate is $8.58 on $5.33 billion in revenues for the coming quarter and $32.98 on $20.31 billion in revenues for the current fiscal year.

AT&T (T) stock lost 14.5% over the month to October 28, 2026, while the S&P 500 gained 1.0%. Its two largest one-day drops, 9.8% on October 9 and 8.0% on October 23, came on news that SpaceX aims to become a major U.S. mobile carrier. Many investors hold AT&T for its 5.6% dividend yield, trusting the shares to fall less than the market in a sell-off and its cash to keep paying the dividend. So when the market sells off, how far has AT&T stock actually fallen before?

How Far Has AT&T Stock Fallen In Past Sell-Offs?

AT&T stock fell as much as 45.0% in the 2008-2009 financial crisis. This marked its deepest drop across market shocks since 2007, while the S&P 500 fell 53.0% over the same dates. The performance fits a wider pattern: across the 14 shocks AT&T traded through, the stock fell 14.0% on average, against a 16.3% decline for the index.

The stock has fallen less than the market on average, but not every time. In the 2023 regional banking crisis, AT&T fell 20.0% while the S&P 500 fell 6.7%.

Recovery times varied widely. From its low, the stock regained its earlier high in a median of 3.4 months, yet four of those recoveries took more than a year. After the financial crisis, the wait was 37.7 months. The falls and recovery times above are measured on past closes that may also count dividends paid.

What Does AT&T Earn, And What Does It Owe?

AT&T earns a wider operating margin than at any time since 2016 and makes enough cash to cover its dividend, but it owes more than it did a year ago. Over the twelve months to September 30, 2026, its operating margin was 21%. That was the highest twelve-month figure at any quarter end since 2016. In the third quarter alone, revenue grew 5.3% from a year earlier.

AT&T produced $17.8 billion of free cash flow over the same twelve months, more than twice the $7.94 billion it paid in dividends. Yet its total debt rose to $178 billion at the end of September, up from $158 billion a year earlier.

AT&T Faces Falling Fiber Prices And Higher Debt

On its October 21, 2026 earnings call, management said average revenue per fiber customer fell 4% from a year earlier in the third quarter. Management tied the fall to introductory prices, discounts for customers who also buy wireless, and lower-priced plans in areas bought from Lumen. It expects a similar decline in the fourth quarter. It also expects higher marketing and customer acquisition costs to weigh on that quarter's adjusted EBITDA growth.

title: What Mattered Most In Comcast's Latest Quarter?
detail:
What Mattered Most In Comcast's Latest Quarter?

Comcast (CMCSA) shares rose 3.4% alongside a 1.2% decline for the S&P 500 on October 22, 2026, the day the company reported its fiscal Q3 2026 results. Earnings per share exceeded the consensus estimate by 5.7%, while revenue fell 2.8% short of its estimate. Those figures cover the entire company. So what did the quarter show about the business behind more than half of Comcast's sales?

Comcast Lost Broadband Customers As Wireless Grew

Management said on the October 22 call that Comcast lost 144,000 broadband subscribers in fiscal Q3 2026 and added 368,000 net wireless lines. Across its home connectivity customers, what management calls convergence revenue fell 2%. Nearly 15% growth in wireless service revenue only partly offset continued pressure on broadband revenue.

Management also said an unusually high number of existing broadband customers on legacy plans moved to new prices during the quarter, increasing churn, the rate at which customers leave. Management said these pricing shifts also weighed on both broadband and wireless customer trends compared with a year earlier.

Comcast posted a slightly smaller report-day gain than its peers. Charter Communications rose 4.2% during the same session, and AT&T and Verizon Communications each gained 3.8%. Between the pre-report close on October 21 and October 28, Comcast shares lost 2.3%, while the S&P 500 was roughly flat.

Comcast's Connectivity Sales Have Slipped For Two Years

These third-quarter broadband losses follow two years of shrinking sales in Residential Connectivity & Platforms, Comcast's largest segment. Revenue for the unit slipped 0.5% in fiscal 2024 and fell by a larger 1.2% in fiscal 2025.

Two other measures showed smaller declines in fiscal Q3 2026. The year-over-year drop in broadband revenue per customer narrowed by 190 basis points from the prior quarter. Similarly, the decline in the connectivity business's EBITDA, an operating profit figure that leaves out depreciation and amortization, narrowed by 140 basis points.

Management expects a further slight improvement in those trends during the fourth quarter, even as Comcast continues moving broadband customers to its new pricing and offering free wireless lines.

What Management Said About Comcast's Broadband Prices

Management said the pressure comes from investments Comcast chose to make, including fundamental changes to its pricing, packaging and customer offerings. It called these moves necessary to position the business for a return to growth over the long term.
